Article Title: Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp, Walt Nauta: 3 aides were allowed with Trump when he was moved into a catering truck during Turkey emergency
Article Text:
Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp and Walt Nauta are the closest aides allowed inside the catering truck that hid President Donald Trump in Turkey.

Who is Dan Scavino?

Who is Natalie Harp?

Who is Walt Nauta?

No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Apart from some low-ranking aides, only three individuals were allowed inside the truck, as they are believed to be the closest to the president: Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations. Washington Post reported that neither Marco Rubio nor Pete Hegseth nor Stephen Miller were allowed inside the truck that took TrumpThe catering truck moved under concealment from the Air Force One aircraft to a smaller Air Force C-32A before flying to Britain separately.Dan Scavino has been serving as the White House deputy chief of staff in the second Trump administration but his history with Trump dates back to 1992, when he worked as a caddie at a New York country club that Trump later purchased and turned into Trump National Golf Club Westchester. After graduating from college, Scavino worked his way up to become the golf club's general manager.He joined Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and went on to serve throughout the entire first Trump administration as White House Director of Social Media and later Deputy Chief of Staff for Communications.During that time, he was particularly known for managing Trump's personal social media presence and online strategy. He remained a central advisor at Mar-a-Lago following the 2020 election, worked as a senior official on the 2024 campaign, and returned to senior White House leadership upon Trump taking office again in 2025.Natalie Harp is an American political aide and former television presenter who serves as Executive Assistant to the President in Donald Trump's second White House administration. She is the one who handles the president's daily schedule and is always spotted with him. Known colloquially among campaign staffers and media outlets as Trump's "human printer," Harp earned a reputation for constantly accompanying him with a portable printer to feed him printed news articles, polls, and favorable commentary. In her role as executive assistant, she remains a member of his inner circle, assisting with his daily schedule and managing dictation for his social media accounts.Walt Nauta is a close political aide to Donald Trump and currently serves in his second White House administration as Deputy Assistant to the President and Director of Oval Office Operations. Nauta spent 20 years in the U.S. Navy, reaching the rank of Senior Chief Petty Officer. During his military career, he was assigned to the Presidential Food Service and eventually became a White House valet during Trump's first presidency. In that role, he acted as a personal assistant and "body man," handling day-to-day tasks like fetching beverages and managing travel details.After Trump left office in 2021, Nauta retired from the Navy and joined Trump's personal staff at Mar-a-Lago, continuing to work as his primary executive assistant and political aide. He later drew widespread national attention when he was indicted alongside Trump in June 2023 in the federal classified documents case, where prosecutors accused him of helping move and conceal boxes of sensitive materials.
Article Summary: No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations, are believed to be the closest aides to the president.

Article Title: Thailand visit, Suu Kyi access: Can Myanmar’s Min Aung Hlaing win political legitimacy?
Article Text:
Min Aung Hlaing in Thailand; Aung San Suu Kyi with ICRC official

Min Aung Hlaing's ascent to power

Significance of Aung San Suu Kyi

Why Thailand visit matters for Min Aung Hlaing - and how Bangkok differs from ASEAN

Can regional engagement help Min Aung Hlaing’s legitimacy push?

Min Aung Hlaing’s continuing legitimacy challenge

Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week, in a trip that carried significance beyond routine diplomacy. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency.That visit to Thailand coincided with another significant development in Myanmar. Aung San Suu Kyi , the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor. On August 3, Suu Kyi met Arnaud de Baecque, the International Committee of the Red Cross' (ICRC) resident representative in her country.Naypyidaw also released photographs of the meeting—the first official images of the former State Counsellor in years.Was the close timing of the two developments just a coincidence? For Min Aung Hlaing, who came to power by overthrowing an elected government rather than through the ballot box, both developments could be part of a broader effort to build political legitimacy and gain wider international acceptance.During his visit to Thailand, the 70-year-old former military leader sought to reassure his host, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, that Myanmar was “returning to democracy.”"Myanmar has now re-established itself on the path to democracy and is moving toward a better future," Min Aung Hlaing told Charnvirakul.The remarks stood in sharp contrast to the circumstances of his rise to the presidency. His claim that Myanmar is on a “democratic path” also comes against the backdrop of a bloody civil war triggered by the coup that brought him to power.According to the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, an independent organisation that documents arrests and casualties linked to the Myanmar civil war, more than 8,200 civilians had been killed and 31,645 people arrested by the regime's security forces as of August 5.Besides, the parliamentary elections under Min Aung Hlaing in late 2025 and early 2026 were also widely criticised as “neither free nor fair” as the army-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party swept the elections, winning 232 of the 263 contested seats in the lower house and 109 of 157 seats in the upper house. Ahead of the presidential election in April—Myanmar's first since 2018—he resigned from the military and was subsequently elected president.However, his transition to the presidency did little to ease international scepticism. Major democracies withheld congratulations following his victory.For Myanmar, Aung San Suu Kyi’s significance extends beyond her role as the head of the country’s first democratically elected civilian government in 50 years and the military’s toppling of her administration.For many inside and outside Myanmar, the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize laureate remains the country's most recognisable symbol of democratic rule and civilian legitimacy.In 2022, Suu Kyi was sentenced to 33 years in prison on a series of charges that her supporters and rights groups described as “politically motivated” and intended to prevent her return to politics. Later, her sentence was reduced to 27 years and, in April, to 18 years, while she was transferred to house arrest.Against this backdrop, the meeting with the ICRC representative was significant because it marked the first confirmed contact between Suu Kyi, 81, and an independent international organisation since her house arrest. It was also her first confirmed communication with the outside world since she wrote a letter to her son from prison in early 2024.Sreeparna Banerjee, an Associate Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation (ORF), agreed that both developments could be seen as part of Myanmar’s broader effort to “manage its international image,” but said it cannot be assumed that the moves were directly linked.“The timing is noteworthy, but it would be difficult to establish a direct connection between the two developments at this stage… Access to Aung San Suu Kyi after a prolonged period of isolation could signal some limited openness, while Min Aung Hlaing’s high-profile visit to Thailand demonstrates Myanmar’s attempt to expand diplomatic engagement,” Banerjee, whose work focuses on Myanmar and Thailand, told The Times of India.For Min Aung Hlaing, the bigger challenge remains turning such diplomatic engagement into wider political legitimacy and international acceptance.According to Banerjee, the visit was important for Min Aung Hlaing because it offered him a degree of political normalisation.“Being received at the highest level by an ASEAN neighbour allows him to project the image of a leader whose government is once again engaging with the region rather than remaining diplomatically isolated,” she said.Significantly, while Thailand and Myanmar are both ASEAN member states, Bangkok’s approach towards Naypyidaw differs from that of the rest of the 11-nation bloc of Southeast Asian states.Thailand has continued to engage with Myanmar despite ASEAN barring Min Aung Hlaing from its top-level meetings over the non-implementation of the Five-Point Consensus agreed with the grouping after he seized power.On this, Banerjee observed that the real value of Bangkok’s “bridge” diplomacy — acting as a bridge between Myanmar and ASEAN — would depend on whether Thailand can use it to encourage some meaningful progress on the Five-Point Consensus.Additionally, ASEAN is yet to recognise the results of Myanmar’s 2025–26 parliamentary elections. The bloc has also repeatedly called for Suu Kyi’s unconditional release, renewing the demand after her meeting with the ICRC official. The regime rebuffed this call too.For its part, Thailand has described its approach vis-à-vis Myanmar as one of “calibrated re-engagement” aimed at keeping dialogue open while responding to “realities on the ground.” Bangkok has also argued that Myanmar is essential to ASEAN unity and regional stability, provided it remains peaceful and stable.In addition to being barred from top-level ASEAN summits, Min Aung Hlaing faces Western sanctions over his role in toppling Suu Kyi’s government, the subsequent civil war, and the alleged persecution of the Rohingya minority in the Rakhine province.The Thailand visit was his fourth overseas trip since becoming president, following visits to India, China, and Laos. India was the only democratic country among the four destinations, underscoring the limited engagement he has so far had with democratic governments.Despite this, and close ties with Russia, he has remained largely isolated internationally.So, can his engagement with Thailand and his wider regional outreach — help him in his bid for greater international recognition and acceptance?Sreeparna Banerjee, the ORF Associate Fellow, suggested that even regional acceptance remains uncertain at this stage, despite such engagement being an important part of Myanmar’s quest for political legitimacy.“Naypyidaw appears determined to engage on its own terms rather than fully follow the ASEAN framework. Thailand's outreach may create space for dialogue, but whether this translates into wider regional acceptance remains uncertain,” she explained.She also highlighted that uncertainty over Myanmar’s regional acceptance stems in part from the fact that Singapore will take over the ASEAN chairmanship in 2027. The city-state has repeatedly called for full implementation of the Five-Point Consensus.This underscores the scale of the challenge facing Min Aung Hlaing in his bid for wider acceptance.For a leader who rises to power as Min Aung Hlaing did, securing international recognition is likely to remain a gradual and difficult process.The regime’s refusal to release Suu Kyi, a global icon, further complicates that effort.Engagement with neighbouring countries can provide an important opening, but broader recognition often depends on how other governments assess the resulting political situation. Yet for Min Aung Hlaing, this remains the only option to secure recognition.For now, engagement with Thailand may offer Min Aung Hlaing some diplomatic space, but whether it can translate into legitimacy for him remains uncertain.
Article Summary: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency. Aung San Suu Kyi, the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor.

Article Title: On parole hearing day, ex-MP Sajjan Kumar, serving life in two 1984 riots cases, dies
Article Text:
Former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar died Thursday while serving life sentences.





NEW DELHI: Former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar, who was serving life sentences in Tihar Jail in two anti-Sikh riots cases, died Thursday. Kumar’s parole hearing was listed in SC on Thursday.Delhi Prisons said Kumar was referred to Safdarjung Hospital for general OPD consultations and age-related ailments, including hypertension, cataract, BPH and Parkinson’s disease. He had been undergoing treatment for these conditions at the same hospital. Around 1.35 pm, Delhi Armed Police personnel reported that Kumar had died at 12.20 pm.“The cause of death will be ascertained in due course,” the statement read. He had been lodged at Tihar since 2018. Safdarjung Hospital, in a statement, said Kumar was brought to the hospital around 11am with altered sensorium. He was immediately admitted and resuscitation measures were initiated.Despite all necessary medical and life-support measures, he could not be revived and was declared dead at 12.30 pm.The hospital said: “He was a known case of hypertension and Parkinson’s disease and had a history of multiple hospital admissions in the past”.There are contradictions in the records regarding Kumar’s age and time of death. Tihar officials stated that he was 80 years old and died at 12.20 pm, while Safdarjung Hospital records put his age at 84 and the time of death at 12.30 pm.Delhi HC sentenced Kumar to life imprisonment in 2018, in a case related to the killing of five Sikhs and the burning of a gurdwara during the anti-Sikh riots that broke out following the assassination of then PM Indira Gandhi by her Sikh bodyguards in 1984.Kumar was also sentenced to life imprisonment in 2025 in another case relating to the killing of two Sikh men during the riots.Kumar was also acquitted in 5 other cases relating to the killing of seven Sikhs in Sultanpuri, with two of these cases currently under appeal.
Article Summary: Former Congress MP Sajjan Kumar was serving life sentences in Tihar Jail in two anti-Sikh riots cases. Kumar’s parole hearing was listed in SC on Thursday. Kumar was referred to Safdarjung Hospital for general OPD consultations and age- related ailments.

Article Title: 'Wait and watch': Lawrence Bishnoi gang claims Hisar court killing of gangster Vinod Panu
Article Text:
Gangster Lawrence Bishnoi has claimed responsibility for the sensational killing of another gangster.





NEW DELHI: Gangster Lawrence Bishnoi has claimed responsibility for the sensational killing of another gangster reported from a court in Hisar, Haryana, on Thursday.The Lawrence group released an audio and a social media post on Friday following the daylight murder of rival gangster Vinod Panu, alias Kana, a high-profile criminal facing over 30 criminal cases, including murder and extortion.Panu was ambushed near the court's parking lot shortly after attending a scheduled hearing. Assailants fired around 14 rounds in rapid succession, critically injuring Panu and two of his associates.Panu later succumbed to his injuries at a nearby hospital. The brazen attack triggered widespread chaos and panic among lawyers, court staff and visitors present on the premises.Shortly after the shooting, a social media message uploaded under the profile name Anil Pandit detailed the motive and named the key perpetrators behind the hit.Transcribed in English, the post reads: "Hail Mahakal, Hail Shri Ram. Greetings to all brothers. The murder of Vinod Panu alias Kana that took place yesterday at Hisar court was executed by me, Himanshu Sonipat. I did this at the instructions of my elder brother Rohit Sonipat, Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu. He considered himself a big gangster and was aligned with our enemies, so he was shown his true place. To all those remaining, listen carefully: mend your ways while there is time, or everyone will meet the same fate.Wait and watch."The statement was accompanied by hashtags referencing allied gang figures.Security personnel and onlookers managed to chase down and arrest one of the armed attackers at the scene, recovering a firearm. Hisar Police have formed six specialised teams to examine forensic evidence, ballistic reports and CCTV footage.Cyber units are currently verifying the authenticity of the post and audio broadcast to trace potential international IP addresses and underlying gang networks.
Article Summary: Lawrence Bishnoi has claimed responsibility for the sensational killing of another gangster reported from a court in Hisar, Haryana, on Thursday. The Lawrence group released an audio and a social media post on Friday following the daylight murder of rival gangster Vinod Panu, alias Kana. Panu was ambushed near the court's parking lot shortly after attending a scheduled hearing.

Article Title: Speeding e-rickshaw kills 10-year-old returning from school in Delhi's Ghazipur
Article Text:
A 10-year-old girl in Delhi was killed when a speeding e-rickshaw (representational image) collided with her, pushing her into the way of an approaching bus.

Priyanshi Bisht,





NEW DELHI: A 10-year-old girl died after a speeding e-rickshaw hit her while she was returning home from school with her mother in east Delhi’s Ghazipur on Thursday afternoon. The impact of the collision was so severe that it threw the child into the path of a bus.Police have registered a case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder and have arrested the accused driver. The victim,a Class 5 student and resident of Khoda Colony in Ghaziabad, was walking home with her mother around 1pm when the accident took place.Her family had moved from a village near Ranikhet in Uttarakhand’s Almora district around eight years ago in search of better educational opportunities for their children.Delhi Police said Priyanshi was walking on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic, while her mother was walking on the inner side, when an e-rickshaw being driven at high speed hit the girl.“The impact was so forceful that Priyanshi was flung forward and rammed into a bus. She suffered a severe head injury,” a police officer said.Her mother and residents rushed her to a hospital, where doctors declared her dead.The driver, identified as Uttam Singh (42), was returning home to Khoda when the accident occurred. Police said he fled after the crash but was traced and arrested. The e-rickshaw has been seized.The family has demanded strict action against the accused, alleging that the e-rickshaw was being driven recklessly. Dinesh Singh Bisht, Priyanshi’s uncle, said the family was looking forward to celebrating Raksha Bandhan together.“She had been excited for Raksha Bandhan. Her younger brother Ayush was eagerly waiting for her to tie him a rakhi. We had all planned to celebrate together, but everything changed in a moment,” he told TOI.He said Priyanshi’s father, Harish Bisht, moved to Delhi in the hope of giving his kids a better future.“My brother works as a helper in a bulb factory and spends whatever he earns on his children’s education. Priyanshi was one of the few in our family to study and her father wanted her to have a proper job. She loved going to school, enjoyed dancing and took part in extracurricular activities. Today, her mother is holding on to nothing but her uniform and shoes,” he said.A case has been registered under Sections 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder) and 281 (rash driving on a public way) of BNS at Ghazipur police station.
Article Summary: A 10-year-old girl died after a speeding e-rickshaw hit her while she was returning home from school. The impact of the collision was so severe that it threw the child into the path of a bus. Police have registered a case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder and arrested the accused driver.

Article Title: Swine flu cases rise amid humid weather; doctors urge caution, respiratory hygiene
Article Text:
Respiratory infections like H1N1 are rising in Delhi-NCR and other regions. (Representational image)

What doctors are seeing

Dengue, H1N1 cases also reported in Delhi

How to protect yourself from H1N1

Cover your mouth and nose with a handkerchief or tissue while coughing or sneezing.

Wash your hands regularly with soap and water or use an alcohol-based hand sanitiser.

Avoid touching your eyes, nose and mouth.

Avoid crowded places where possible.

Keep some distance from people with flu-like symptoms.

Get adequate rest, sleep and fluids, and eat nutritious food.

Dispose of used tissues properly and disinfect reusable handkerchiefs.

Shake hands or hug others when you are unwell.

Take medicines without consulting a doctor.

Meet relatives and friends if you have flu-like symptoms.

When to seek medical help

(With inputs from ANI)





NEW DELHI: H1N1 ( swine flu ) and other respiratory infections are being reported more frequently in Delhi-NCR and some other parts of the country amid humid and variable weather conditions, with doctors advising people to watch for flu-like symptoms and take precautions to prevent the spread of infection.Doctors said seasonal illnesses such as influenza, commonly referred to as swine flu, tend to increase during the monsoon. Vulnerable groups, including elderly people, young children and those with existing health conditions, may be at greater risk of complications.AIIMS Delhi professor of medicine Dr Neeraj Nischal said common cold, influenza and other viral infections causing respiratory symptoms are frequently seen during the season.Symptoms can include a runny nose, cough, fever, body aches and fatigue. He said people with conditions such as COPD or asthma, as well as the elderly and those with other comorbidities, need to be particularly cautious.Dr Manohar KN, lead consultant in internal medicine and diabetology at SPARSH Hospital in Bengaluru, said his hospital was also seeing an increase in seasonal H1N1 cases.Around five to six patients a day were reporting flu-related symptoms at the hospital, with two to three patients being admitted, he said.Dr Harpreet Kaur of Aakash Healthcare said the hospital had recorded both dengue and H1N1 cases in July, with H1N1 cases increasing significantly in August.She said stagnant water during the monsoon can favour mosquito breeding, while damp and humid conditions can facilitate the spread of respiratory infections, particularly indoors and in crowded settings.Asian Hospital's Dr Sunil Rana said his hospital was also seeing dengue, swine flu and H3N2 cases, with symptoms ranging from cough and throat pain to severe pneumonia.Doctors advised people to maintain basic respiratory hygiene and avoid spreading infection to others.Dos:Don'ts:Doctors said mild cases may be managed with symptomatic treatment, while some patients, particularly those in vulnerable groups, may require hospital care if respiratory symptoms become severe.Vaccines are also available for influenza, and doctors advised high-risk groups to discuss vaccination with their healthcare providers.
Article Summary: H1N1 and other respiratory infections are being reported more frequently in Delhi-NCR and some other parts of the country. Doctors said seasonal illnesses such as influenza, commonly referred to as swine flu, tend to increase during the monsoon. Doctors advised people to maintain basic respiratory hygiene and avoid spreading infection to others.

Article Title: 22-year-old stabbed to death in Kalyanpuri, 2 injured, 2 held
Article Text:
New Delhi:





A 22-year-old man was stabbed to death, and two of his relatives were injured during an altercation in east Delhi ’s Kalyanpuri early Thursday. Two people have been apprehended in connection with the incident.The deceased, Jay Singh, was a resident of Kalyanpuri. Police said the incident took place on the road between 11 and 15 Blocks, around 12.46 am.A police team reached the spot and found that Singh was rushed to Lal Bahadur Shastri Hospital, where he was declared brought dead. Two of Singh’s relatives, who also sustained injuries, were taken for medical treatment.Speaking to reporters, a relative of Singh claimed that an argument had ensued between two groups and he had been called to intervene and resolve the matter. She added that Singh is survived by his wife and 10-day-old child.A police inquiry revealed that the altercation stemmed from a disagreement during an ongoing function. “A group of transgender people had come in at the function. An argument had ensued between the family and the group which later on escalated into a scuffle. During this, one trans person was slapped, which led to further escalation,” said a senior police officer.Singh’s last rites were also reportedly conducted amid tight security, with Delhi Police personnel deployed in the area to prevent any further confrontation. A case has been registered at Kalyanpuri police station. Police have seized the knife used in the offence. The two apprehended accused and others who were present at the function are being questioned.
Article Summary: Jay Singh, 22, was stabbed to death in east Delhi's Kalyanpuri. Two of his relatives were injured in the altercation. Two people have been apprehended in connection with the incident. A police inquiry revealed that the altercation stemmed from a disagreement during an ongoing function.
